questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: In acidic medium, one mole of dichromate ion (Cr₂O₇²⁻) oxidises how many moles of Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺?
questions.explanation: Each Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to 2Cr³⁺, which gains 6 electrons. Each Fe²⁺ loses one electron on oxidation to Fe³⁺, so 6 moles of Fe²⁺ are oxidised per mole of dichromate.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Potassium dichromate

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Which catalyst is used in the Contact process for manufacturing sulphuric acid?
questions.explanation: In the Contact process, sulphur dioxide is oxidised to sulphur trioxide over vanadium(V) oxide. V₂O₅ works because vanadium switches between +5 and +4 oxidation states, which is typical of d-block catalysts. TiCl₄ belongs to Ziegler–Natta catalysis.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Catalytic properties of transition elements

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Which of the following is an interstitial compound of a transition metal?
questions.explanation: Interstitial compounds form when small non-metal atoms such as carbon, nitrogen, hydrogen or boron occupy the voids in a metal lattice. TiC is the example here, and such compounds are hard, have high melting points and retain metallic conductivity.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Interstitial compounds

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: In aqueous solution Cu⁺ disproportionates, while Cu²⁺ is stable. The main reason is:

options.text: The high hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ more than compensates for the second ionisation enthalpy of copper
Cu⁺ has a higher hydration enthalpy than Cu²⁺
Cu⁺ has a half-filled d subshell
Cu⁺ is a stronger oxidising agent than Cu²⁺

questions.explanation: Cu⁺ is 3d¹⁰ and disproportionates as 2Cu⁺ → Cu + Cu²⁺. The Cu²⁺ ion has a very large hydration enthalpy, which offsets the energy needed to remove the second electron from copper, so Cu²⁺ is more stable in water.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Stability of copper oxidation states

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Actinoids show a wider range of oxidation states than lanthanoids. The main reason is:

options.text: 5f electrons are more effectively shielded than 4f electrons
Actinoid ions have lower ionisation enthalpies than lanthanoid ions
Actinoids have no electrons in 6d orbitals
The 5f, 6d and 7s energy levels are close, so more electrons take part in bonding

questions.explanation: The 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals have similar energies, so several electrons can be used in bonding. The 5f electrons are less effectively shielded than 4f electrons, and this allows a wider spread of oxidation states than in the lanthanoids.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Actinoids

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: In an acidic medium, MnO₄⁻ is reduced to Mn²⁺. How many moles of MnO₄⁻ are needed to oxidise 2.5 mol of Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺?
questions.explanation: Each MnO₄⁻ gains five electrons to become Mn²⁺, and each Fe²⁺ gives one electron. So 2.5 mol of Fe²⁺ supplies 2.5 mol of electrons, and 2.5 ÷ 5 = 0.5 mol of MnO₄⁻ is required.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Potassium permanganate

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed with inert electrodes. The products formed are:

options.text: H₂ at the anode and Na at the cathode
Cl₂ at the anode and H₂ at the cathode
O₂ at the anode and Na at the cathode
Cl₂ at the cathode and H₂ at the anode

questions.explanation: At the cathode, water is reduced to H₂ and OH⁻, which is easier than reducing Na⁺. At the anode, chloride ions are oxidised to Cl₂ in concentrated solution, which is preferred over oxidising water to O₂.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Electrolytic cells and Faraday laws

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Iron is galvanised by coating it with a metal so that the coating protects iron even when the surface is scratched. The metal is:
questions.explanation: Zinc has a more negative standard electrode potential (−0.76 V) than iron (−0.44 V), so it corrodes first and acts as a sacrificial anode. A tin or nickel coating protects only while it is intact.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Corrosion

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: The standard electrode potential of Zn²⁺/Zn is −0.76 V. At 298 K, the potential of the Zn²⁺/Zn electrode in 0.1 M Zn²⁺ solution is closest to (take 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V):
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation, E = E° − (0.059/n) log(1/[Zn²⁺]) with n = 2. So E = −0.76 − (0.059/2) × log 10 = −0.76 − 0.03 = −0.79 V.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Nernst equation

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: For a cell reaction with n = 2, the standard EMF is 0.59 V at 298 K. Taking 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V, the equilibrium constant K is approximately:
questions.explanation: At equilibrium E = 0, so the Nernst equation gives log K = nE°/0.059. Here log K = (2 × 0.59)/0.059 = 20, so K ≈ 10²⁰.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Relation between EMF and equilibrium constant

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: During discharge of a lead storage battery, the density of the sulphuric acid electrolyte:
questions.explanation: Discharge gives Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄ → 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O. Sulphuric acid is consumed and water is produced, so the electrolyte becomes more dilute and its density falls. Checking the density is how the battery state is judged.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Batteries: lead storage battery

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: The conductivity of a 0.02 M solution of an electrolyte is 0.0024 S cm⁻¹ at 298 K. Its molar conductivity, in S cm² mol⁻¹, is:
questions.explanation: Molar conductivity is Λm = κ × 1000 / c, where c is in mol L⁻¹. So Λm = 0.0024 × 1000 / 0.02 = 120 S cm² mol⁻¹, which is 1.2 × 10².
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Molar conductivity

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: The quantity of electricity needed to deposit 21.6 g of silver (molar mass 108 g mol⁻¹) from a solution of Ag⁺ is closest to (F = 96500 C mol⁻¹):
questions.explanation: Moles of Ag = 21.6 / 108 = 0.2 mol, and each Ag⁺ needs one electron. So Q = 0.2 × 96500 = 19 300 C, which is 1.9 × 10⁴ C, as given by Faraday first law.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Faraday laws of electrolysis

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Among Li, K, Na and Mg, which metal is the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution? (Standard potentials: Li⁺/Li −3.05 V, K⁺/K −2.93 V, Na⁺/Na −2.71 V, Mg²⁺/Mg −2.37 V)
questions.explanation: The most negative standard reduction potential means the metal is most easily oxidised, so it is the strongest reducing agent. Lithium is at −3.05 V, even though potassium is more reactive in air, because the Li⁺ ion is strongly hydrated in water.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Standard electrode potential series

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Kohlrausch law gives the limiting molar conductivity of NH₄OH as λ°(NH₄Cl) + λ°(NaOH) − λ°(NaCl). With λ°(NH₄Cl) = 150.0, λ°(NaOH) = 248.0 and λ°(NaCl) = 126.5 (S cm² mol⁻¹), Λ°m(NH₄OH) is closest to:
questions.explanation: Kohlrausch law gives Λ°m(NH₄OH) = 150.0 + 248.0 − 126.5 = 271.5 S cm² mol⁻¹, which is 2.7 × 10² to two significant figures. The law applies to each ion independently at infinite dilution.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Kohlrausch law

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: A concentration cell is Ag | Ag⁺ (0.1 M) || Ag⁺ (0.001 M) | Ag at 298 K. Taking 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V, its EMF is closest to:
questions.explanation: The cell EMF is E = (0.059/n) log(c_cathode / c_anode). Reduction happens at the 0.1 M electrode, so E = 0.059 × log(0.1/0.001) = 0.059 × 2 = 0.118 V, which is 0.12 V.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Nernst equation: concentration cells

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: A solution with 0.1 mol Ag⁺ and 0.1 mol Cu²⁺ is electrolysed with inert electrodes, and 0.15 F of charge is passed with 100% current efficiency. The mass of copper deposited is closest to (Ag = 108, Cu = 63.5 g mol⁻¹):
questions.explanation: Ag⁺ is reduced first, because it has the higher reduction potential (+0.80 V). Its 0.1 mol takes 0.1 F, so 0.05 F is left for Cu²⁺. That gives 0.05 / 2 = 0.025 mol Cu, which is 0.025 × 63.5 ≈ 1.6 g.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Electrolytic cells and Faraday laws

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: The chelate effect makes [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ more stable than [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺. The main thermodynamic reason is:

options.text: en is a stronger field ligand with a larger Δo
The enthalpy of formation of [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ is much larger
The number of particles increases on chelation, giving a positive entropy change
Chelating ligands have a lower coordination number

questions.explanation: In [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺ + 3 en → [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ + 6 NH₃, the number of particles rises from 4 to 7. This gives a positive entropy change, which makes the chelate complex more stable. The enthalpy change is similar for both complexes.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 5 Coordination Compounds, Chelate effect and stability of complexes

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: The crystal field stabilisation energy of the high-spin octahedral [Cr(H₂O)₆]²⁺ ion (a d⁴ ion) is:
questions.explanation: Water is a weak-field ligand, so the complex is high spin: t₂g³ e_g¹. CFSE = 3(−0.4 Δo) + 1(+0.6 Δo) = −0.6 Δo. The eg electron adds +0.6 Δo, which is why the answer is not −1.2 Δo.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 5 Coordination Compounds, Crystal field theory
